original_value: Wireless, flexible, ion-selective electrodes (ISEs) are of great interest in the development of wearable health monitors and clinical systems. Existing film-based electrochemical sensors, however, still have practical limitations due to poor electrical contact and material–interfacial leakage. Here, we introduce a wireless, flexible film-based system with a highly selective, stable, and reliable sodium sensor. A flexible and hydrophobic composite with carbon black and soft elastomer serves as an ion-to-electron transducer offering cost efficiency, design simplicity, and long-term stability. The sensor package demonstrates repeatable analysis of selective sodium detection in saliva with good sensitivity (56.1 mV/decade), stability (0.53 mV/h), and selectivity coefficient of sodium against potassium (−3.0). The film ISEs have an additional membrane coating that provides reinforced stability for the sensor upon mechanical bending. Collectively, the comprehensive study of materials, surface chemistry, and sensor design in this work shows the potential of the wireless flexible sensor system for low-profile wearable applications.

result.paraphrase: Wireless, flexible ion-selective electrodes (ISEs) are attracting considerable attention for wearable health monitoring and clinical applications. However, conventional film-based electrochemical sensors still face practical drawbacks stemming from poor electrical contact and material-interface leakage. In this work, we present a wireless, flexible film-based system featuring a highly selective, stable, and reliable sodium sensor. The ion-to-electron transducer is a flexible, hydrophobic carbon black/soft elastomer composite, providing low cost, simple design, and long-term stability. The sensor package enables repeatable selective sodium detection in saliva with good sensitivity (56.1 mV/decade), stability (0.53 mV/h), and a sodium-to-potassium selectivity coefficient of −3.0. In addition, the film ISEs include a membrane coating that enhances stability when the sensor is mechanically bent. Overall, this study of materials, surface chemistry, and sensor design demonstrates the potential of the wireless flexible sensor system for low-profile wearable use.
